scenario.title: Meeting Room Reservation
scenario.initial_description: A meeting room is reserved for a team meeting. The organizer checks availability and shares the room information with participants.

reference_workflow.goal: Reserve an appropriate meeting room and notify participants with room details.

activities.name: Collect meeting time and participant count
Select room matching capacity and equipment needs

decisions.condition: Does the meeting require special equipment?

automation_opportunities.rationale: Availability checks can be automated through calendar and reservation APIs.
Room selection can be rule-based using capacity, location, and equipment constraints.
Calendar invitation updates can be automated after reservation.

activities.name: Cancel or Rebook Room
outputs: Cancellation confirmation or new booking reference

decisions.condition: Is a suitable room available for the required date, time, and capacity?
branches: Yes - Proceed to Select Suitable Room (A3)
No - Adjust requirements or choose different date/time, return to A1

decisions.condition: Has the participant count changed significantly after responses are received?
Has the meeting been cancelled or rescheduled?

exceptions: Room becomes unavailable after reservation due to double booking or system error
Organizer forgets to release room after meeting cancellation
Room booking system is offline or inaccessible
Required equipment not available in selected room
Participant list is incomplete or contains incorrect contact information
Meeting time conflict discovered after invitations are sent
Room capacity exceeded by late-added participants

automation_opportunities.rationale: Room availability lookup is a repetitive, rule-based query against calendar and booking data. It can be fully automated to return real-time availability without manual searching.
constraints: Room booking system must expose an API or have query capabilities
Calendar data must be up-to-date and centralized

automation_opportunities.rationale: Once a room is selected, the reservation action is a structured transaction that can be automated via API calls to the booking system, reducing manual data entry and errors.
constraints: Booking system must support automated reservation via API or integration
Conflict detection must be handled in real time

automation_opportunities.target: A5 - Send Room Information to Participants
automation_opportunities.rationale: Notification to participants can be automated by triggering calendar invites or emails upon booking confirmation, eliminating manual communication steps.
constraints: Integration between booking system and email or calendar platform required
Participant contact data must be available and accurate

automation_opportunities.rationale: Pre-meeting reminders are time-based and rule-driven, making them ideal for automated scheduling triggered at defined intervals before the meeting.
constraints: Email or calendar system must support scheduled automated notifications
Reminder timing rules must be configurable

automation_opportunities.target: D1 - Is a suitable room available?
automation_opportunities.rationale: Availability filtering and decision-making based on capacity, equipment, and time constraints can be automated using rule-based logic applied to booking system data.
constraints: Room attributes must be structured and maintained in the booking system
Logic rules must be predefined and maintained

automation_opportunities.target: D2 - Has participant count changed significantly?
automation_opportunities.rationale: Response tracking and threshold comparison can be automated by monitoring RSVP status and comparing accepted attendees against room capacity rules.
constraints: Calendar or email platform must expose RSVP status data
Threshold definition requires organizational policy input

automation_opportunities.rationale: If participant count changes are detected automatically, the system can trigger room re-evaluation and update or suggest alternate rooms without organizer intervention.
constraints: Requires full integration between RSVP tracking and booking system
Organizer approval may still be needed for room changes

automation_opportunities.rationale: Cancellation workflows can be partially automated by detecting meeting cancellation signals from calendar systems and triggering room release automatically.
constraints: Calendar cancellation must be detectable by booking system via event or webhook
Rebooking requires availability data and may need organizer confirmation

assumptions: A centralized room booking system exists and maintains real-time calendar data for all rooms.
Rooms have structured metadata including capacity, available equipment, and location.
The organization uses a standard email or calendar platform that supports invitations and RSVP tracking.
The organizer has the authority to reserve rooms without additional approval for standard team meetings.
Participant contact information is maintained in a directory accessible to the organizer.
Meeting reminders are considered standard practice and participants expect them.
Room reservations are made in advance, providing sufficient lead time for automation to function.
Cancellations or reschedules are communicated through the same calendar or email platform used for invitations.
No financial approval or cost center allocation is required for standard internal room bookings.
The booking system can generate unique booking reference IDs for each reservation.

missing_information.gap: No system or tool identified for checking room availability (e.g., calendar platform, booking portal, or facility management system)
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without knowing the system used, it is impossible to assess integration feasibility or determine if an API or automation hook exists for availability checks

missing_information.gap: No mention of whether a facility manager, admin, or automated system is involved in confirming or approving the reservation
missing_information.why_it_matters: If a human approver is required, this adds a manual step that may be a bottleneck and a prime automation target

missing_information.gap: No logic defined for what happens when the desired room is unavailable (e.g., suggest alternative room, alternative time, escalate)
missing_information.why_it_matters: This decision branch is critical for automation design; without it, the automated flow cannot handle the most common exception

missing_information.gap: No handling described for conflicts such as double bookings, last-minute cancellations, or room capacity mismatches
missing_information.why_it_matters: Exception handling gaps lead to incomplete automation and potential process failures that require manual intervention

missing_information.gap: No specification of required reservation inputs (e.g., meeting duration, number of attendees, required equipment, recurrence pattern)
missing_information.why_it_matters: These inputs determine the booking rules and validation logic needed to automate the reservation accurately

missing_information.gap: The method and content of sharing room information with participants is undefined (e.g., calendar invite, email notification, chat message)
missing_information.why_it_matters: The communication step may involve multiple systems and must be specified to automate end-to-end participant notification

missing_information.gap: No indication of how often meeting room reservations occur, or whether they are recurring or ad hoc
missing_information.why_it_matters: Frequency determines the automation ROI and whether a self-service or batch automation approach is more appropriate

missing_information.gap: No estimate of the time or steps currently required to complete the reservation process manually
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without a manual effort baseline, it is difficult to quantify automation savings or prioritize this process for investment

missing_information.gap: No information on whether room reservation is linked to other processes such as catering requests, AV setup, or visitor access provisioning
missing_information.why_it_matters: Upstream or downstream dependencies affect the scope of automation and may require cross-system orchestration

missing_information.gap: It is unclear whether a master room inventory with attributes (capacity, equipment, location) is maintained and accessible digitally
missing_information.why_it_matters: Automation of availability checks and matching requires structured, accessible room data; absence of this data blocks automation

clarification_questions.question: What system or tool is currently used to check room availability and make reservations — for example, a calendar application, a dedicated room booking portal, or a facility management system?

When the desired meeting room is unavailable for the requested time, what is the current process — does the organizer manually search for alternatives, or is there a rule-based suggestion mechanism in place?
What information does the organizer need to provide when making a reservation, such as meeting duration, number of attendees, required equipment, or recurrence?

How is the room information shared with participants after the reservation is confirmed — through a calendar invite, email, instant messaging, or another channel — and is this step done manually today?
Are there any approval steps or roles involved in confirming a room reservation, such as a facility manager or administrative coordinator, or is the booking self-service?
Is the meeting room reservation process ever connected to other requests such as catering, AV equipment setup, or visitor badge access, and if so, how are those triggered today?
